steps.title: UI tour
steps.intro: Produced by tools/render_jobs/jobs/ui_tour.json with probes/ui_primitives.gd: every top screen at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 window sizes (names start with the size), for the tt-sim-ui-critic agent (docs/UI_TASTE.md). A 100 ft temperate forest map is saved as the test level _ui_tour_room (shown as Mossy Hollow) for authoring, play and the host's room, and deleted at the end. The session screens are staged by probes/ui_room.gd without a network (nothing is hosted or joined): the Opening a room... wait (Root's loading overlay over the title, scrimmed, its bar gliding), the room (RoomPanel) from a staged session summary as the GM sees it with a shelf of three maps and four players, with no map at all, and as a player sees it, the join screen as the title's Join Game opens it, the room drawer over the table as the GM sees it, and in play the pause menu as the host sees it (the host-only Return everyone to the room row, shown on a solo pause) and the confirmation that row asks. The map_load_ captures show Root's loading overlay for a map load: map_load_title and map_load_table staged mid-load over the title and over a live table (the probe's map_load action; nothing is loaded), map_load_real a real load of the test map caught about 0.4 s after Play. focus_paper and focus_glass show keyboard focus on a quiet button of each theme leaf, and focus_selected_card and focus_selected_tile focus on a selected item, where the focus ring and the selection must both read (drawer tiles take no focus in the game; the probe lets the picked one); the dusk_ captures repeat the in-play screens with the time of day set to 19:00 through the Sun pane. Then the Interface size passes (probes/ui_size.gd): 1366x768 at Auto (1.35, an 800 px canvas) and a 1920x1080 window at a fixed 150% (named 1920x1080@150, a 1280x720 canvas), each with the title, Settings Graphics, the new-map dialog as it opens and scrolled to its end, and the play Visuals drawer; at 1280x720 (Auto 1.40) the Interface Size dropdown open and a staged measure line over the board. Last, one ultrawide probe capture.
